observed: The released Service<RoleServer> dispatcher capability-gates GetTaskRequest, UpdateTaskRequest, and CancelTaskRequest, then calls the corresponding ServerHandler methods.

The released ServerHandler get_task method accepts GetTaskParams plus RequestContext<RoleServer> and returns Result<GetTaskResult, McpError>; its default is method-not-found. The released cancel_task method likewise accepts CancelTaskParams plus RequestContext<RoleServer> and returns Result<(), McpError>; its default is method-not-found.

Those public handler signatures do not contain TaskManager or TaskContext, so an application can override them and read/update its own persisted task records without routing those requests through stock TaskManager memory.

The exact task model exposes Task::new(task_id,status,created_at,last_updated_at), DetailedTask::new(task,payload), and GetTaskResult::new(detailed_task). TaskAckResult::new() is the released complete-result acknowledgement model for tasks/update and tasks/cancel; the server dispatcher maps the handler's unit result to a task acknowledgement.

DetailedTask forces base task status to match TaskPayload, and deserialization fails when status-specific payload such as inputRequests/result/error is missing, giving a useful fail-closed serialization boundary for a persisted store adapter.
finding.inference: Within the exact rmcp-v3.1.4 released server trait/model surface, serving already-persisted task state through tasks/get and accepting cooperative tasks/cancel does not require stock TaskManager. An application-owned durable store can implement the public ServerHandler methods and construct the released result models directly.
finding.scope_limit: This proves only the public serving/acknowledgement seam. It does not prove caller-stable task creation, atomic create-or-get, durable scheduling, restart redrive, task-result exactly-once behavior, or external-effect idempotency/fencing. It also does not yet pin the exact released field/constructor definitions of GetTaskParams, CancelTaskParams, or UpdateTaskParams.
